summary: New sense 1b: beglückwünschen, gratulieren (zur Hochzeit; belegt mit k-Formen);

data.label: 1b
data.gloss: beglückwünschen, gratulieren (zur Hochzeit; belegt mit k-Formen);

rationale: Guests visit, eat, congratulate the couple and leave, whereas clergy perform the rite with x-forms. This recurring social action is distinguished by the Turoyo narrative roles and sequence; its brx/brk etymological filing remains a question.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infinitiv (JTM 1.3/12)

data.turoyo: <...> falge d bəroxo kməḥšu, bəṯr məd mṣalele lu qašo, w twiro i ṭlamṯaṯe baynoṯayye.
data.translation: <...> Es gilt als die halbe Trauung, wenn der Priester gebetet hat und dieser Brotfladen zwischen ihnen gebrochen worden ist.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infinitiv cell, sense 2: the event noun denotes a marriage rite and is qualified as half-completed.

data.translation: <...> Sie teilen das Essen aus, dann kommen ihre Gäste, essen, beglückwünschen den Bräutigam und gehen.

rationale: New subsense 1b: guests congratulate the groom as one act in a social visiting sequence.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (JTM 1.3/41)

data.translation: Sie kommen und gratulieren dem Bräutigam und der Braut, man bewirtet sie mit Süßigkeiten, und jeder legt sein Geldgeschenk auf das Tablett, auf dem ihm Süßigkeiten angeboten wurden. <...>

rationale: New subsense 1b: both spouses are explicit objects, with gifts and hospitality establishing a congratulatory visit.

data.translation: <...> Wenn es später Nachmittag geworden ist, alle zu Abend gegessen haben und das Essen vorbei ist, dann holen sie den Priester und die Diakone. Die einen bringen (das Brautpaar) zur Kirche und trauen sie (dort), die anderen (machen die Trauung) im Haus.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (MAC Besim Martyrdom of Maferyono/8)

data.turoyo: Qām lu+ăġà dəmmina, qrele lu+Mafәryono. Ašə́r lu+Mafәryono məḷḷe, ‘Yani, hīč dasṫər bi+ʕito lu+medano lə+kowe!’ ḥatta məḷḷe, ‘Yani, d̥owe hnoste, u+aḥuno ŭ i+ḥoṯo komibarxi, elo u+qariwo ŭ i+qarito, d̥kətne qariwone, dasṫər bu+medano layto’.
data.translation: The agha, let’s say, up and summoned the maphrian. Really, the maphrian said, ‘That is, by no means is there ever permission in the church for this thing!’ He even said, ‘That is, even if it were a whatsit, the brother and the sister get married, but a godbrother and a godsister, who are godsiblings, there isn’t any permission for this thing’.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell: coordinated brother/sister subject and prohibition context; edition wording retained without endorsing its social claim.

summary: New idiom: barəx mor ‘Segne, Herr!’ (feste kirchliche Grußformel)

data.turoyo: Barəx mor, miḥasina ba ṣlawoṯayḏux.
data.translation: Segne uns Huerr! Mögen wir durch deine Gebete erlöst werden.

rationale: Lookup search barəx found no existing formula; fixed ecclesiastical request is documented here rather than used to posit a productive bare stem-II Imperativ. Compare JTM 4.3/8, PrS 55/2 and 47/18.

summary: II.2 denotes clerical solemnization, with a priest/molla and a bride or couple object; II.3 denotes arranging a marriage or one's own marriage. ʕal is common but neither its presence nor the edition's heiraten alone distinguishes the two. At 24/108 the pair and ʕal ḥḏoḏe allow either arrangement or rite; retained II.2 provisionally.

The k-forms gəmbarki/kəmbarki/kəmbarkənne in JTM 1.3 concern congratulatory visits, gifts and hospitality, contrasting local x-forms with clergy. Their lexical social function warrants provisional 1b under brx II; the consulted brk entry contains only kneeling, not congratulations. The reader's claim that tabrik occurs in each verse is wrong: it is present only in /49.

tabrik at JTM 1.3/49 is an Arabic-shaped event noun with lu- and a genitive dependent; it supports the social interpretation but is not counted as a productive Turoyo Infinitiv. Arabic mbārak/mbarak xilxālik/šāšik at JTM 4.4/21 is a quoted formula, not secure native II morphology.

Barəx mor is a fixed church greeting; bare Barəx alone does not establish a productive native stem or missing form. 66/279 explicitly labels its hymn as Classical Syriac; its six brx records are comparative only and yield no Turoyo box examples.

I Part. Pass. blessings show brixo with feminine themes (PrS 11/21, 16/52, 42/108, 53/36), regular brəxto (26/245), and quantified plural brixe (64/144–152, 89/126, 107/119). The reader's feminine singular analysis of brixe at 64/148 is not accepted. These are not additional lexical senses.

II Detransitive Infectum depicts a couple entering marriage, including reciprocal ʕal ḥḏoḏe, without specifying an external agent. The Detransitive Infinitiv label for beroxo follows the existing entry convention, not an independently proved Detransitive derivation of the event noun.

The six compact occurrence records contain no verse. Their classifications are retained provisionally without pretending to recheck omitted text. Alignment-flagged 88/308 and both 112/355 tokens contribute no quoted translation or example.

Are the wedding-congratulation k-forms in JTM 1.3 Arabic loans under brk II or variants appropriate under brx II? Verify 1b's root filing; tabrik alone does not settle it. At /49 what is the antecedent and number of -nne?

Please verify mbarxile at JTM 1.3/37 and lo+mbarxile at MAC Besim Martyrdom of Maferyono/9. The /9 form permits Preterit singular agent/plural patient or Infectum plural agent/singular object; its past context alone does not resolve the morphology.
Does the fixed greeting Barəx mor belong only among Syriac-derived idioms or also in a native Imperativ box? The added formula preserves Talay's printed Huerr.

At 62/342 does Mbarxole retain the priest from /341, or introduce the husband? II.2 is provisional. Confirm similarly the arranger/officiant subject at MAC NI Fingan Agha and Sultan Hasan/67 and 98/29.

Are brixo with feminine themes and quantified brixe invariant formulae or transcription/agreement variants? Preserve alfo=brixe, mo brixe and šawʕi brixe. 107/119 translates šawʕi as Hundertmal; no numeral correction is made.
Verify printed mbarazto at 70/119 against mbaraxto at 70/79; no new regular form or brz sense is inferred.

Existing citation 47/19 attached to bazar and explicit aʕlox blessings does not match the supplied verse, which says Aloho mbarəx without either complement. Existing prs 27/2 versus matching PrS 11/21 and LB 14 versus Talay 1/14 may reflect source numbering; confirm before replacing inherited references. The 37/14 citation attached to the Gulo phrase supplies beroxo but not that phrase.

52/173 has no German for Brixe elux. At 88/308 alignment flags an inserted German audience aside. At 112/355 both brixe tokens occur in embedded 356, whose German is missing; the flag's description of that continuation is itself inaccurate. No flagged or missing translation is quoted.
